sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- mcp: MCP gateway — install by URL, status, search, describe, auth, and single MCP tool calls
- mcp__openstreetmap: MCP namespace proxy for openstreetmap

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

<project_instructions path="C:\Users\linco\Desktop\profile-generation\AGENTS.md">
# Repository instructions

These guidelines apply to work across this repository. For profile-generation tasks, use the detailed workflow and schema in [`.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md`](.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md) as the source of truth. For CSV population, follow [`.pi/synthetic-profile-population/SKILL.md`](.pi/synthetic-profile-population/SKILL.md) and its format reference. This file adds repository-wide guidance; it does not replace or redefine those workflows.

## Project structure

- `scripts/news_context.py` discovers news and extracts article text. Keep its CLI and `fetch_news_context` Python API behavior consistent when changing it.
- `src/profile_generation/` contains the installable Python package.
- `.pi/` contains agent prompts, skills, references, and their helper scripts.
- `profiles/` is the destination for generated profile CSV files.
- `README.md` documents setup and common workflows; update it when user-facing commands or repository structure change.

## Development

- Use Python 3.15 or newer and `uv` for dependency management. Declare runtime dependencies in `pyproject.toml` and keep `uv.lock` in sync when dependencies change.
- Run commands from the repository root unless a task requires otherwise.
- Keep changes focused and follow the existing style of the file being edited.
- For Python changes, run a focused check such as `uv run python -m py_compile <file>` and any relevant available tests. Do not claim tests passed unless they were run.

## Generated profile data

- Follow the profile fields, balance, and output location specified by the profile-generation prompt; do not silently change its schema or requirements.
- Profile records must be synthetic, not represented as real records. Use the project’s country-specific randomized ID/phone templates documented in the profile prompt; note that they are mock templates, not verified official formats or guaranteed unassigned values. Email addresses must end in `.com`; provider or company domains may be deliverable or coincide with real mailboxes. Use a unique UUID for `profile_id`.
- The CSV helper flattens nested profile objects into underscore-separated columns and stores lists as JSON text. Keep the profile field set consistent so every appended row matches the existing CSV columns.

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.description: Convert every profile row in a CSV file into one JSON array using the nested profile schema. Use when asked to get all user profiles.

csv_path.description: CSV file path relative to the workspace root; defaults to profiles/users.csv.

toolsAdded.name: mcp
toolsAdded.description:
MCP gateway — URL installation, server status, tool search/describe, auth, and single MCP tool calls. When a user supplies an MCP endpoint URL, install it with the install action. Non-MCP Pi tools should be called directly, not through mcp.

Servers: openstreetmap

Usage:
  mcp({ action: "install", url: "https://example.com/mcp" }) → Install, connect, and authenticate an MCP URL
  mcp({ })                              → Show server status and tool counts
  mcp({ server: "name" })               → List tools from server
  mcp({ search: "query" })              → Search MCP tools by name/description
  mcp({ describe: "tool_name" })        → Show tool details and parameters
  mcp({ instructions: "name" })         → Show full server usage instructions
  mcp({ connect: "server-name" })       → Connect to a server and refresh metadata
  mcp({ tool: "name", args: { key: "value" } })         → Call a tool (object args; JSON string also accepted)
  mcp({ action: "ui-messages" })        → Retrieve accumulated messages from completed UI sessions
  mcp({ action: "save-script", args: { name, description, code, inputSchema } }) → Save a script as a reusable tool (asks you first)
  mcp({ action: "auth-start", server: "name" })      → Open OAuth and watch for completion
  mcp({ action: "auth-complete", server: "name", args: { redirectUrl: "..." } }) → Complete manual OAuth

Mode: action > tool (call) > connect > describe > instructions > search > server (list) > nothing (status)

args.description: Tool arguments as a JSON object, or as a JSON string encoding one

connect.description: Server name to connect (lazy connect + metadata refresh)

instructions.description: Server name to show that server's usage instructions

searchMode.description: Search backend (default: lexical; semantic ranks tools by meaning with a Pi classifier model)

regex.description: Treat search as regex (default: substring match)

includeSchemas.description: Include parameter schemas in search results (default: true)

server.description: Server name: filters searches, disambiguates calls and describe operations, and optionally names an install

cancelTask.description: Stop a background MCP task by its <server>/<taskId> key

toolsAdded.name: web_search
toolsAdded.description: Search the web for real-time information using your local Ollama instance's web_search API. Requires Ollama running locally with web search enabled.

max_results.description: Maximum number of search results to return (default: 5)

toolsAdded.name: web_fetch
toolsAdded.description: Fetch and extract text content from a web page URL using your local Ollama instance's web_fetch API. Requires Ollama running locally with web fetch enabled.

url.description: URL to fetch and extract content from

toolsAdded.name: mcp__openstreetmap
toolsAdded.description: Namespace-proxy for MCP server "openstreetmap". Forwards `{tool, args}` through the adapter's executeCall, so it inherits the same auth / lifecycle / output-guard rules as the `mcp` proxy.

tool.description: Underlying MCP tool name to call on this server.

args.description: Arguments for the underlying tool. When mcp is available, use mcp({ search: '...' }) to inspect schemas; for unique names use mcp({ describe: 'tool_name' }) with the exact tool name returned by search.

toolsAdded.description:
MCP gateway — URL installation, server status, tool search/describe, auth, and single MCP tool calls. When a user supplies an MCP endpoint URL, install it with the install action. Non-MCP Pi tools should be called directly, not through mcp.

Servers: openstreetmap

Usage:
  mcp({ action: "install", url: "https://example.com/mcp" }) → Install, connect, and authenticate an MCP URL
  mcp({ })                              → Show server status and tool counts
  mcp({ server: "name" })               → List tools from server
  mcp({ search: "query" })              → Search MCP tools by name/description
  mcp({ describe: "tool_name" })        → Show tool details and parameters
  mcp({ instructions: "name" })         → Show full server usage instructions
  mcp({ connect: "server-name" })       → Connect to a server and refresh metadata
  mcp({ tool: "name", args: { key: "value" } })         → Call a tool (object args; JSON string also accepted)
  mcp({ action: "ui-messages" })        → Retrieve accumulated messages from completed UI sessions
  mcp({ action: "save-script", args: { name, description, code, inputSchema } }) → Save a script as a reusable tool (asks you first)
  mcp({ action: "auth-start", server: "name" })      → Open OAuth and watch for completion
  mcp({ action: "auth-complete", server: "name", args: { redirectUrl: "..." } }) → Complete manual OAuth

Mode: action > tool (call) > connect > describe > instructions > search > server (list) > nothing (status)

# Profile generation

This repository contains agent instructions for creating synthetic user profiles, a Python news-context scraper to gather current regional context, and a helper for appending profile records to CSV files.

## Requirements and installation

- Python 3.15 (the required version is recorded in `.python-version` and `pyproject.toml`)
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) for environment and dependency management

From the repository root, install the project and its dependencies:

```powershell
uv sync
```

`uv.lock` pins the resolved dependencies. The news script uses Requests, Beautiful Soup, and Readability; `uv sync` installs them from `pyproject.toml`.

## How profile generation works

Profile generation is currently driven by agent instructions rather than an implemented Python generation command:

1. Gather relevant news context for each needed region and language with [`scripts/news_context.py`](scripts/news_context.py).
2. Follow the profile-generation prompt in [`.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md`](.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md) to create profiles in the specified JSON-object format.
3. Append each profile to a CSV under `profiles/` with the population helper described below.

The installed `profile-generation` command currently only prints a greeting; it does not generate profiles.

## News context script

Run commands from the repository root. For example, to retrieve one Swahili article for Kenya:

```powershell
uv run scripts/news_context.py --language sw --region Kenya --max-articles 1
```

The script prints progress messages while discovering and extracting candidate pages, then prints the formatted article context. It defaults to one output article. Use `--max-articles N` to request more.

Options:

- `--language`: required; `en`, `sw`, or `am`
- `--region`: optional region or country, such as `Kenya` or `East Africa`
- `--theme`: optional profile domain: `work`, `travel`, `school`, `shopping`, `family`, or `daily_planning`
- `--category`: optional news category, such as `business`, `politics`, `sports`, or `health`
- `--query`: optional search phrase that helps discover and rank articles; it does not strictly filter results
- `--strict-region`: skip extracted articles whose body does not mention the requested region
- `--max-articles`: number of articles to include; defaults to `1`

For example, focus on education news:

```powershell
uv run scripts/news_context.py --language sw --region Kenya --theme school
```

The configured publishers are Taifa Leo, The Standard (Kenya), and BBC. Publisher availability depends on language, and results should be checked for relevance to the requested region—particularly for North America, which has no dedicated source configured.

The module can also be called from Python:

```python
from scripts.news_context import fetch_news_context

result = fetch_news_context(
    language="sw",
    region="Kenya",
    theme="school",
    max_articles=1,
)
print(result["text"])                 # formatted full-text context
print(result["details"]["articles"])  # article metadata
```

## Run a question bank through Pi JSON mode

Use [src/main.py](src/main.py) to start the multi-turn runs from the command line. Select one user with `--uuid` or every user with `--all-users`. By default all categories run; pass `--category` to select a category (repeat it for more than one):

```powershell
uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001
uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001 --category school
uv run python src\main.py --all-users --category travel --category school
```

Each selected question is passed as a positional prompt to one Pi process in JSON mode, in category and question-bank order. The runner streams Pi's JSONL events to stdout and appends them to `sessions\<user_id>.jsonl`, one file per user. It prints the exact log path before each run. Set `GEMINI_API_KEY` before running. By default, logs are saved in the project `sessions` folder. Choose another folder with `--session-dir` or `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`.

```powershell
uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001 --category school --session-dir .\sessions
```

The same runner is available from Python. Pass categories to run only selected categories, or omit `categories` to process all six:

```python
from scripts.spawn_user_session import run_user_question_bank

questions_by_category = run_user_question_bank(
    "101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001",
    categories=["school"],
)
```

The function reads `data/synthetic_conversation_starter.json`, passes all selected questions in one invocation, and returns the selected category-to-questions mapping. JSONL events are streamed to stdout and appended to the per-user session file; the API key is read from `GEMINI_API_KEY` by default. `run_category_questions(user_id, category)` remains available for running just one category.

## Repository agent files (`.pi/`)

- [`.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md`](.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md) defines the profile-generation workflow, regional sample balance, expected profile fields, and domain-specific guidance. It accepts a CSV name as its argument and targets `profiles/$1.csv`.
- [`.pi/synthetic-profile-population/SKILL.md`](.pi/synthetic-profile-population/SKILL.md) describes the CSV population helper workflow.
- [`.pi/synthetic-profile-population/references/formats.md`](.pi/synthetic-profile-population/references/formats.md) documents the expected profile object shape.
- [`.pi/synthetic-profile-population/scripts/populate.py`](.pi/synthetic-profile-population/scripts/populate.py) reads one nested JSON object from standard input, flattens nested dictionaries into underscore-separated CSV columns, and appends the row. It creates the file and headers if needed, and requires later objects to flatten to the same columns.

Append one profile JSON object per helper invocation:

```powershell
'{"profile_id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","identifiers":{"first_name":"Amina","last_name":"Example","email":"amina.0001+001@gmail.com","phone_number":null,"national_id":null,"national_id_format_note":"Synthetic mock format; not verified as an official identifier format.","country":"Kenya"},"personal_attributes":{"age":34,"location":"Nairobi, Kenya","occupation":"Teacher","education_level":"Bachelor degree","family_status":"Single","health_condition":"None"},"domain_metadata":{"primary_domain":"school","active_scenarios":["school","daily_planning"]}}' |
  uv run .pi/synthetic-profile-population/scripts/populate.py profiles\profiles.csv
```

The helper does not generate profile attributes or verify identities, but it fills null `phone_number` and `national_id` fields with random numbers following the project’s mock templates: Kenya ID 11 digits starting `40`; Tanzania ID 10 digits; Ethiopia ID 10 digits starting `392`; US state-ID-style mock 10 digits. Phone templates use `+254`, `+255`, `+251`, or `+1` plus the national digits described in the profile prompt. These are user-provided examples, not verified government or telephone allocations, and values are not guaranteed to be unassigned. The helper validates the schema and templates, including an exact integer for `age` and email addresses ending in `.com`. Addresses at provider or company domains may be deliverable or coincide with real mailboxes. The resulting columns include `identifiers_first_name`, `identifiers_national_id_format_note`, `personal_attributes_location`, and `domain_metadata_primary_domain`. Lists such as `active_scenarios` are stored as JSON text in a single cell. Invalid records are rejected with a non-zero exit status.
The UUID above is only an example; generate a new unique UUID for every row.

## OpenStreetMap MCP server

The project MCP configuration is in [`.pi/mcp.json`](.pi/mcp.json), and the stdio server is [`.pi/openstreetmap_mcp.py`](.pi/openstreetmap_mcp.py). It provides `search_places` and `reverse_geocode` tools using a Nominatim-compatible endpoint. The configuration defaults to a local Nominatim instance at `http://localhost:8080`; set `NOMINATIM_URL` in the configuration to an endpoint you are authorized to use.

Use the tools only for individual, user-requested lookups. Do not use autocomplete, bulk or systematic queries, or submit personal or confidential data. Requests are limited to one per second. Returned map data includes OpenStreetMap attribution; review the [Nominatim usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/) before configuring a public endpoint.

## Project layout

```text
.pi/
  prompts/                         Agent prompt for profile generation
  mcp.json                         OpenStreetMap MCP client configuration
  openstreetmap_mcp.py             OpenStreetMap MCP server
  synthetic-profile-population/    Agent skill, format reference, CSV helper
profiles/                          Generated profile CSV files
scripts/
  news_context.py                  News discovery and full-text extraction
src/profile_generation/            Python package entry point
pyproject.toml                     Project metadata and dependencies
uv.lock                            Locked dependency versions
```

## Environment variables

Set these in PowerShell from the repository root before running conversations:

```powershell
$env:GEMINI_API_KEY = "your-gemini-api-key"
$env:PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR = "$($PWD.Path)\sessions"
$env:PI_MAX_TURNS = "50"

uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001
```

- `GEMINI_API_KEY` is required for Gemini model requests.
- `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` sets where per-user JSONL conversation files are saved. The command above uses the repository's `sessions` folder.
- `PI_MAX_TURNS` sets Pi's maximum turns to `50`.

These settings apply to the current PowerShell window. Set them again in a new window before running the command.

# Profile generation

This repository contains agent instructions for creating synthetic user profiles, a Python news-context scraper to gather current regional context, and a helper for appending profile records to CSV files.

## Requirements and installation

- Python 3.15 (the required version is recorded in `.python-version` and `pyproject.toml`)
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) for environment and dependency management

From the repository root, install the project and its dependencies:

```powershell
uv sync
```

`uv.lock` pins the resolved dependencies. The news script uses Requests, Beautiful Soup, and Readability; `uv sync` installs them from `pyproject.toml`.

## How profile generation works

Profile generation is currently driven by agent instructions rather than an implemented Python generation command:

1. Gather relevant news context for each needed region and language with [`scripts/news_context.py`](scripts/news_context.py).
2. Follow the profile-generation prompt in [`.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md`](.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md) to create profiles in the specified JSON-object format.
3. Append each profile to a CSV under `profiles/` with the population helper described below.

The installed `profile-generation` command currently only prints a greeting; it does not generate profiles.

## News context script

Run commands from the repository root. For example, to retrieve one Swahili article for Kenya:

```powershell
uv run scripts/news_context.py --language sw --region Kenya --max-articles 1
```

The script prints progress messages while discovering and extracting candidate pages, then prints the formatted article context. It defaults to one output article. Use `--max-articles N` to request more.

Options:

- `--language`: required; `en`, `sw`, or `am`
- `--region`: optional region or country, such as `Kenya` or `East Africa`
- `--theme`: optional profile domain: `work`, `travel`, `school`, `shopping`, `family`, or `daily_planning`
- `--category`: optional news category, such as `business`, `politics`, `sports`, or `health`
- `--query`: optional search phrase that helps discover and rank articles; it does not strictly filter results
- `--strict-region`: skip extracted articles whose body does not mention the requested region
- `--max-articles`: number of articles to include; defaults to `1`

For example, focus on education news:

```powershell
uv run scripts/news_context.py --language sw --region Kenya --theme school
```

The configured publishers are Taifa Leo, The Standard (Kenya), and BBC. Publisher availability depends on language, and results should be checked for relevance to the requested region—particularly for North America, which has no dedicated source configured.

The module can also be called from Python:

```python
from scripts.news_context import fetch_news_context

result = fetch_news_context(
    language="sw",
    region="Kenya",
    theme="school",
    max_articles=1,
)
print(result["text"])                 # formatted full-text context
print(result["details"]["articles"])  # article metadata
```

## Run a question bank through Pi JSON mode

Use [src/main.py](src/main.py) to start the multi-turn runs from the command line. Select one user with `--uuid` or every user with `--all-users`. By default all categories run; pass `--category` to select a category (repeat it for more than one):

```powershell
uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001
uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001 --category school
uv run python src\main.py --all-users --category travel --category school
```

Each selected question is passed as a positional prompt to one Pi process in JSON mode, in category and question-bank order. The runner streams Pi's JSONL events to stdout and appends them to `sessions\<user_id>.jsonl`, one file per user. It prints the exact log path before each run. Set `GEMINI_API_KEY` before running. By default, logs are saved in the project `sessions` folder. Choose another folder with `--session-dir` or `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`.

```powershell
uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001 --category school --session-dir .\sessions
```

The same runner is available from Python. Pass categories to run only selected categories, or omit `categories` to process all six:

```python
from scripts.spawn_user_session import run_user_question_bank

questions_by_category = run_user_question_bank(
    "101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001",
    categories=["school"],
)
```

The function reads `data/synthetic_conversation_starter.json`, passes all selected questions in one invocation, and returns the selected category-to-questions mapping. JSONL events are streamed to stdout and appended to the per-user session file; the API key is read from `GEMINI_API_KEY` by default. `run_category_questions(user_id, category)` remains available for running just one category.

## Repository agent files (`.pi/`)

- [`.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md`](.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md) defines the profile-generation workflow, regional sample balance, expected profile fields, and domain-specific guidance. It accepts a CSV name as its argument and targets `profiles/$1.csv`.
- [`.pi/synthetic-profile-population/SKILL.md`](.pi/synthetic-profile-population/SKILL.md) describes the CSV population helper workflow.
- [`.pi/synthetic-profile-population/references/formats.md`](.pi/synthetic-profile-population/references/formats.md) documents the expected profile object shape.
- [`.pi/synthetic-profile-population/scripts/populate.py`](.pi/synthetic-profile-population/scripts/populate.py) reads one nested JSON object from standard input, flattens nested dictionaries into underscore-separated CSV columns, and appends the row. It creates the file and headers if needed, and requires later objects to flatten to the same columns.

Append one profile JSON object per helper invocation:

```powershell
'{"profile_id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","identifiers":{"first_name":"Amina","last_name":"Example","email":"amina.0001+001@gmail.com","phone_number":null,"national_id":null,"national_id_format_note":"Synthetic mock format; not verified as an official identifier format.","country":"Kenya"},"personal_attributes":{"age":34,"location":"Nairobi, Kenya","occupation":"Teacher","education_level":"Bachelor degree","family_status":"Single","health_condition":"None"},"domain_metadata":{"primary_domain":"school","active_scenarios":["school","daily_planning"]}}' |
  uv run .pi/synthetic-profile-population/scripts/populate.py profiles\profiles.csv
```

The helper does not generate profile attributes or verify identities, but it fills null `phone_number` and `national_id` fields with random numbers following the project’s mock templates: Kenya ID 11 digits starting `40`; Tanzania ID 10 digits; Ethiopia ID 10 digits starting `392`; US state-ID-style mock 10 digits. Phone templates use `+254`, `+255`, `+251`, or `+1` plus the national digits described in the profile prompt. These are user-provided examples, not verified government or telephone allocations, and values are not guaranteed to be unassigned. The helper validates the schema and templates, including an exact integer for `age` and email addresses ending in `.com`. Addresses at provider or company domains may be deliverable or coincide with real mailboxes. The resulting columns include `identifiers_first_name`, `identifiers_national_id_format_note`, `personal_attributes_location`, and `domain_metadata_primary_domain`. Lists such as `active_scenarios` are stored as JSON text in a single cell. Invalid records are rejected with a non-zero exit status.
The UUID above is only an example; generate a new unique UUID for every row.

## OpenStreetMap MCP server

The project MCP configuration is in [`.pi/mcp.json`](.pi/mcp.json), and the stdio server is [`.pi/openstreetmap_mcp.py`](.pi/openstreetmap_mcp.py). It provides `search_places` and `reverse_geocode` tools using a Nominatim-compatible endpoint. The configuration defaults to a local Nominatim instance at `http://localhost:8080`; set `NOMINATIM_URL` in the configuration to an endpoint you are authorized to use.

Use the tools only for individual, user-requested lookups. Do not use autocomplete, bulk or systematic queries, or submit personal or confidential data. Requests are limited to one per second. Returned map data includes OpenStreetMap attribution; review the [Nominatim usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/) before configuring a public endpoint.

## Project layout

```text
.pi/
  prompts/                         Agent prompt for profile generation
  mcp.json                         OpenStreetMap MCP client configuration
  openstreetmap_mcp.py             OpenStreetMap MCP server
  synthetic-profile-population/    Agent skill, format reference, CSV helper
profiles/                          Generated profile CSV files
scripts/
  news_context.py                  News discovery and full-text extraction
src/profile_generation/            Python package entry point
pyproject.toml                     Project metadata and dependencies
uv.lock                            Locked dependency versions
```

## Environment variables

Set these in PowerShell from the repository root before running conversations:

```powershell
$env:GEMINI_API_KEY = "your-gemini-api-key"
$env:PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR = "$($PWD.Path)\sessions"
$env:PI_MAX_TURNS = "50"

uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001
```

- `GEMINI_API_KEY` is required for Gemini model requests.
- `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` sets where per-user JSONL conversation files are saved. The command above uses the repository's `sessions` folder.
- `PI_MAX_TURNS` sets Pi's maximum turns to `50`.

These settings apply to the current PowerShell window. Set them again in a new window before running the command.

# Profile generation

This repository contains agent instructions for creating synthetic user profiles, a Python news-context scraper to gather current regional context, and a helper for appending profile records to CSV files.

## Requirements and installation

- Python 3.15 (the required version is recorded in `.python-version` and `pyproject.toml`)
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) for environment and dependency management

From the repository root, install the project and its dependencies:

```powershell
uv sync
```

`uv.lock` pins the resolved dependencies. The news script uses Requests, Beautiful Soup, and Readability; `uv sync` installs them from `pyproject.toml`.

## How profile generation works

Profile generation is currently driven by agent instructions rather than an implemented Python generation command:

1. Gather relevant news context for each needed region and language with [`scripts/news_context.py`](scripts/news_context.py).
2. Follow the profile-generation prompt in [`.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md`](.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md) to create profiles in the specified JSON-object format.
3. Append each profile to a CSV under `profiles/` with the population helper described below.

The installed `profile-generation` command currently only prints a greeting; it does not generate profiles.

## News context script

Run commands from the repository root. For example, to retrieve one Swahili article for Kenya:

```powershell
uv run scripts/news_context.py --language sw --region Kenya --max-articles 1
```

The script prints progress messages while discovering and extracting candidate pages, then prints the formatted article context. It defaults to one output article. Use `--max-articles N` to request more.

Options:

- `--language`: required; `en`, `sw`, or `am`
- `--region`: optional region or country, such as `Kenya` or `East Africa`
- `--theme`: optional profile domain: `work`, `travel`, `school`, `shopping`, `family`, or `daily_planning`
- `--category`: optional news category, such as `business`, `politics`, `sports`, or `health`
- `--query`: optional search phrase that helps discover and rank articles; it does not strictly filter results
- `--strict-region`: skip extracted articles whose body does not mention the requested region
- `--max-articles`: number of articles to include; defaults to `1`

For example, focus on education news:

```powershell
uv run scripts/news_context.py --language sw --region Kenya --theme school
```

The configured publishers are Taifa Leo, The Standard (Kenya), and BBC. Publisher availability depends on language, and results should be checked for relevance to the requested region—particularly for North America, which has no dedicated source configured.

The module can also be called from Python:

```python
from scripts.news_context import fetch_news_context

result = fetch_news_context(
    language="sw",
    region="Kenya",
    theme="school",
    max_articles=1,
)
print(result["text"])                 # formatted full-text context
print(result["details"]["articles"])  # article metadata
```

## Run a question bank through Pi JSON mode

Use [src/main.py](src/main.py) to start the multi-turn runs from the command line. Select one user with `--uuid` or every user with `--all-users`. By default all categories run; pass `--category` to select a category (repeat it for more than one):

```powershell
uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001
uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001 --category school
uv run python src\main.py --all-users --category travel --category school
```

Each selected question is passed as a positional prompt to one Pi process in JSON mode, in category and question-bank order. The runner streams Pi's JSONL events to stdout and appends them to `sessions\<user_id>.jsonl`, one file per user. It prints the exact log path before each run. Set `GEMINI_API_KEY` before running. By default, logs are saved in the project `sessions` folder. Choose another folder with `--session-dir` or `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`.

```powershell
uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001 --category school --session-dir .\sessions
```

The same runner is available from Python. Pass categories to run only selected categories, or omit `categories` to process all six:

```python
from scripts.spawn_user_session import run_user_question_bank

questions_by_category = run_user_question_bank(
    "101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001",
    categories=["school"],
)
```

The function reads `data/synthetic_conversation_starter.json`, passes all selected questions in one invocation, and returns the selected category-to-questions mapping. JSONL events are streamed to stdout and appended to the per-user session file; the API key is read from `GEMINI_API_KEY` by default. `run_category_questions(user_id, category)` remains available for running just one category.

## Repository agent files (`.pi/`)

- [`.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md`](.pi/prompts/generate-profiles.md) defines the profile-generation workflow, regional sample balance, expected profile fields, and domain-specific guidance. It accepts a CSV name as its argument and targets `profiles/$1.csv`.
- [`.pi/synthetic-profile-population/SKILL.md`](.pi/synthetic-profile-population/SKILL.md) describes the CSV population helper workflow.
- [`.pi/synthetic-profile-population/references/formats.md`](.pi/synthetic-profile-population/references/formats.md) documents the expected profile object shape.
- [`.pi/synthetic-profile-population/scripts/populate.py`](.pi/synthetic-profile-population/scripts/populate.py) reads one nested JSON object from standard input, flattens nested dictionaries into underscore-separated CSV columns, and appends the row. It creates the file and headers if needed, and requires later objects to flatten to the same columns.

Append one profile JSON object per helper invocation:

```powershell
'{"profile_id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","identifiers":{"first_name":"Amina","last_name":"Example","email":"amina.0001+001@gmail.com","phone_number":null,"national_id":null,"national_id_format_note":"Synthetic mock format; not verified as an official identifier format.","country":"Kenya"},"personal_attributes":{"age":34,"location":"Nairobi, Kenya","occupation":"Teacher","education_level":"Bachelor degree","family_status":"Single","health_condition":"None"},"domain_metadata":{"primary_domain":"school","active_scenarios":["school","daily_planning"]}}' |
  uv run .pi/synthetic-profile-population/scripts/populate.py profiles\profiles.csv
```

The helper does not generate profile attributes or verify identities, but it fills null `phone_number` and `national_id` fields with random numbers following the project’s mock templates: Kenya ID 11 digits starting `40`; Tanzania ID 10 digits; Ethiopia ID 10 digits starting `392`; US state-ID-style mock 10 digits. Phone templates use `+254`, `+255`, `+251`, or `+1` plus the national digits described in the profile prompt. These are user-provided examples, not verified government or telephone allocations, and values are not guaranteed to be unassigned. The helper validates the schema and templates, including an exact integer for `age` and email addresses ending in `.com`. Addresses at provider or company domains may be deliverable or coincide with real mailboxes. The resulting columns include `identifiers_first_name`, `identifiers_national_id_format_note`, `personal_attributes_location`, and `domain_metadata_primary_domain`. Lists such as `active_scenarios` are stored as JSON text in a single cell. Invalid records are rejected with a non-zero exit status.
The UUID above is only an example; generate a new unique UUID for every row.

## OpenStreetMap MCP server

The project MCP configuration is in [`.pi/mcp.json`](.pi/mcp.json), and the stdio server is [`.pi/openstreetmap_mcp.py`](.pi/openstreetmap_mcp.py). It provides `search_places` and `reverse_geocode` tools using a Nominatim-compatible endpoint. The configuration defaults to a local Nominatim instance at `http://localhost:8080`; set `NOMINATIM_URL` in the configuration to an endpoint you are authorized to use.

Use the tools only for individual, user-requested lookups. Do not use autocomplete, bulk or systematic queries, or submit personal or confidential data. Requests are limited to one per second. Returned map data includes OpenStreetMap attribution; review the [Nominatim usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/) before configuring a public endpoint.

## Project layout

```text
.pi/
  prompts/                         Agent prompt for profile generation
  mcp.json                         OpenStreetMap MCP client configuration
  openstreetmap_mcp.py             OpenStreetMap MCP server
  synthetic-profile-population/    Agent skill, format reference, CSV helper
profiles/                          Generated profile CSV files
scripts/
  news_context.py                  News discovery and full-text extraction
src/profile_generation/            Python package entry point
pyproject.toml                     Project metadata and dependencies
uv.lock                            Locked dependency versions
```

## Environment variables

Set these in PowerShell from the repository root before running conversations:

```powershell
$env:GEMINI_API_KEY = "your-gemini-api-key"
$env:PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR = "$($PWD.Path)\sessions"
$env:PI_MAX_TURNS = "50"

uv run python src\main.py --uuid 101a4b2c-1101-4a01-8b01-000000000001
```

- `GEMINI_API_KEY` is required for Gemini model requests.
- `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` sets where per-user JSONL conversation files are saved. The command above uses the repository's `sessions` folder.
- `PI_MAX_TURNS` sets Pi's maximum turns to `50`.

These settings apply to the current PowerShell window. Set them again in a new window before running the command.
